summary:
We developed Project E.D.E.N. It is a smart system that connects astronaut health directly to the spacecraft's plant greenhouse.

Our software works like a "living pharmacy." If it sees that an astronaut has a health problem—like high stress or weak bones—it immediately tells them exactly what plant they need to grow to feel better.

Before planting, our system checks the spacecraft's seed vault. Space radiation can damage seeds, so our software makes sure to select only the safe, healthy ones. It tells the crew exactly which medical seed pod to plug into the NASA Veggie greenhouse so it is guaranteed to grow.

Why is this important? NASA already has health sensors and space greenhouses, but they are not connected. E.D.E.N. is the missing software that links them together so the crew can survive 100% on their own. Because in deep space, your spacecraft must also be your caregiver.
details:
We built Project E.D.E.N. as a completely autonomous dashboard to solve a major gap in space health. NASA already has the Human Research Program (HRP) gathering data from wearables like Bio-Monitor shirts, and they have greenhouses like the Veggie system. However, these tools do not talk to each other. E.D.E.N. is the software and hardware bridge that connects them without needing constant human control.

Because our focus is preventative medicine, we don't wait for an astronaut to get sick. The autonomous dashboard tracks health data to catch early warning signs, like rising stress or bone loss. Once it spots a trend, it acts as a proactive botanical system. It automatically prescribes a specific plant to give the crew the exact nutrients they need to stop the illness from ever happening.

We knew space radiation destroys seed DNA, so our software required a hardware concept. We integrated our dashboard with a 3D digital design of a seed pod preservation and dispensing machine. Our dashboard audits the digital seed vault, finds a radiation-safe pod, and visually commands the 3D-modeled machine to release it. In a real-world application, the crew would simply take this cartridge and plug it straight into the NASA Veggie system.

This approach solves major space travel problems. First, it saves a lot of payload weight and money since seeds are much lighter than heavy medical supplies. Second, in deep space, astronauts can't wait for doctors on Earth to send instructions. E.D.E.N. gives them 100% independence through continuous preventative care. We also realized this has a huge impact on Earth, as isolated communities could use our autonomous system to grow their own natural preventative treatments locally.

During the hackathon, we coded the dashboard using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, linked it to a Supabase database, and designed the 3D models using Spline on an HP EliteBook. We feel our project is highly creative because we didn't invent fake, magic wearables. We took real, existing NASA hardware and built the missing pieces to turn a basic space garden into an autonomous health and prevention system.
